prompt: What product does ethyl acetate give when treated with sodium ethoxide in ethanol, then H3O+?

choices.why: In a Claisen condensation the tetrahedral intermediate expels ethoxide instead of being protonated, so the product is a ketone, not an alcohol.
The product keeps a ketone carbonyl group from the acceptor ester; it is a β-keto ester.
One ethoxy group leaves as ethanol, so the product has only one ester group.

explanation: This is the Claisen condensation: two molecules of ethyl acetate combine, with loss of ethanol, to give the β-keto ester ethyl acetoacetate in 75% yield.

prompt: Ethyl acetate is C4H8O2. How many hydrogen atoms does ethyl acetoacetate, its Claisen condensation product, contain?
explanation: Two ethyl acetate molecules (C8H16O4) combine and lose one molecule of ethanol (C2H6O), giving C6H10O3, CH3COCH2CO2CH2CH3. It has 16 − 6 = 10 hydrogens.

prompt: What is the only difference between the mechanism of an aldol condensation and that of a Claisen condensation?

choices.text: The fate of the tetrahedral intermediate: in the Claisen reaction it expels an alkoxide ion
The fate of the tetrahedral intermediate: in the Claisen reaction it is protonated to an alcohol
choices.why: Protonation to an alcohol happens in the aldol reaction. In the Claisen reaction an alkoxide leaving group is expelled.

choices.text: The Claisen reaction goes through an enol rather than an enolate ion
choices.why: Both reactions involve nucleophilic addition of an enolate ion to a carbonyl group.

choices.text: In the Claisen reaction the enolate adds to the α carbon of the second ester
choices.why: In both reactions the enolate adds to the carbonyl carbon of the second partner.

explanation: Both reactions start with nucleophilic addition of an enolate ion to a carbonyl group. In the aldol reaction the tetrahedral intermediate is protonated to give an alcohol; in the Claisen reaction it expels an alkoxide to give an acyl substitution product.

prompt: What small molecule is lost when two molecules of an ethyl ester undergo a Claisen condensation?

choices.why: Water is lost when an aldol product dehydrates. In a Claisen condensation the leaving group is ethoxide, which ends up as ethanol.
No carbon is lost as CO2; the product keeps the acyl group and the ester group.
The acyl group stays in the product; only the ethoxy part leaves, as ethanol.

explanation: The Claisen condensation of an ester results in loss of one molecule of alcohol, ethanol for ethyl esters, and an acyl group of one reactant bonds to the α carbon of the second.

prompt: How many equivalents of base, such as sodium ethoxide, are used in a Claisen condensation of an ester like ethyl acetate?
explanation: The β-keto ester product has a highly acidic, doubly activated hydrogen that the base removes, so a full equivalent of base is needed rather than a catalytic amount.

prompt: Why does a Claisen condensation of an ester with more than one acidic α hydrogen require a full equivalent of base?

choices.text: The base removes an acidic hydrogen from the β-keto ester product
Esters are not acidic at all, so extra base is needed
choices.why: Esters, like aldehydes and ketones, are weakly acidic; the extra base is used up deprotonating the product.

choices.text: A full equivalent is needed to keep the reaction reversible
choices.why: Deprotonating the product does the opposite: it drives the equilibrium completely to the product side.

choices.text: The base is needed to protonate the tetrahedral intermediate
choices.why: A base removes protons. The tetrahedral intermediate expels an alkoxide ion.

explanation: If the starting ester has more than one acidic α hydrogen, the β-keto ester product has a highly acidic, doubly activated hydrogen that base removes. That uses a full equivalent of base, and it drives the equilibrium to the product side, so yields are usually high.

prompt: Ethyl propanoate, CH3CH2CO2Et, has five carbon atoms. How many carbon atoms does its Claisen condensation product contain?
explanation: Two ethyl propanoate molecules have 10 carbons. The Claisen condensation loses one ethanol (2 carbons), leaving 8: ethyl 2-methyl-3-oxopentanoate, CH3CH2COCH(CH3)CO2Et.

prompt: What product forms from the Claisen condensation of ethyl propanoate, CH3CH2CO2Et (Worked Example 23.7.1)?

choices.why: The α carbon of ethyl propanoate carries a methyl group, so the product has a methyl branch on carbon 2.
In a Claisen condensation the tetrahedral intermediate expels ethoxide, giving a ketone, not an alcohol.
That has an acetyl group, which would come from ethyl acetate. Here the acyl group added is propanoyl, CH3CH2CO–.

explanation: The propanoyl group of one ester bonds to the α carbon of the second, and ethanol is lost. The product is the β-keto ester ethyl 2-methyl-3-oxopentanoate.

prompt: What product would you expect from the Claisen condensation of ethyl butanoate, CH3CH2CH2CO2Et?

choices.why: The α carbon of ethyl butanoate carries an ethyl group, so the product is branched at carbon 2.
The tetrahedral intermediate expels ethoxide, so carbon 3 becomes a ketone carbonyl, not an alcohol.
That has an acetyl group. The acyl group transferred from ethyl butanoate is butanoyl, CH3CH2CH2CO–.

explanation: The butanoyl group of one ester bonds to the α carbon of the second, which carries an ethyl group, and ethanol is lost. The product is the β-keto ester ethyl 2-ethyl-3-oxohexanoate.

prompt: The Claisen reaction is reversible. What does ethyl benzoylacetate, C6H5COCH2CO2Et, give when it is cleaved by sodium hydroxide in ethanol (Exercise 23.7.2)?

choices.why: The bond that breaks is between the ketone carbonyl carbon and the α carbon; the benzoyl part becomes benzoate and the –CH2CO2Et part becomes ethyl acetate.
The benzoyl carbonyl carbon ends up as a carboxylate, benzoate, not an aldehyde.
The benzoyl group must end up in one of the fragments; ethyl acetate has no phenyl group.

explanation: Because the Claisen reaction is reversible, a β-keto ester can be cleaved by base into two fragments by the exact reverse of the forward mechanism. Ethyl benzoylacetate gives benzoate ion and ethyl acetate.
